expectations.text: Uses ContainerModule methods for hiding the back button and refresh button
expectations.evidence: response.md section 1 shows `await container.hideBackButton();` and `await container.hideRefreshButton();`, and the 'Putting it together' code block calls both `container.hideBackButton()` and `container.hideRefreshButton()`. Both methods exist verbatim on ContainerModule in src/modules/container/ContainerModule.ts (lines 254-276 and 362-384) with matching zero-argument signatures and 204/500/501 status codes.

expectations.text: Uses ContainerModule to set the title and/or background color
expectations.evidence: response.md section 2 shows `await container.setTitle('Checkout');` and `await container.setBackgroundColor('#0A0A0A');`, repeated in the combined example. Both methods exist verbatim on ContainerModule (ContainerModule.ts lines 140-165 setBackgroundColor, 200-222 setTitle), taking a single string parameter (hex color / title text) as shown in the response.

expectations.text: Uses ContainerModule.sendAnalyticsEvent (or equivalent) to fire an analytics event
expectations.evidence: response.md section 3 and the combined example call `await container.sendAnalyticsEvent({ state: ContainerAnalyticsEventState.CHECKOUT_PAGE, name: 'DEFAULT' });`. This matches the real API: sendAnalyticsEvent is defined in ContainerModule.ts (lines 806-838) taking a { state, name, data? } request, and ContainerAnalyticsEventState.CHECKOUT_PAGE / the 'DEFAULT' name are real exported constants in src/modules/container/constants.ts (lines 16-33).

claims.claim: container.hideBackButton() / hideRefreshButton() are the methods to hide the native back/refresh buttons, with showBackButton()/showRefreshButton() as counterparts
claims.evidence: All four methods exist on ContainerModule with matching no-arg signatures (ContainerModule.ts lines 254-438).

claims.claim: setBackgroundColor controls the title bar's color and takes a hex string
claims.evidence: ContainerModule.ts docstring: 'Set the background color of the container header... hex format, e.g., "#ffffff"' (lines 108-116), matching response's use of '#0A0A0A'.

claims.claim: sendAnalyticsEvent's 'name' field can be the literal string 'DEFAULT' and is described as the 'standard system event' for page loads
claims.evidence: ContainerAnalyticsEventName.DEFAULT = 'DEFAULT' exists in constants.ts line 32. The response uses the literal string 'DEFAULT' rather than importing/referencing the ContainerAnalyticsEventName constant, which is a minor style inconsistency (it imports ContainerAnalyticsEventState but not ContainerAnalyticsEventName) but is functionally correct since the enum's value is the same string.

claims.claim: CHECKOUT_PAGE is 'the journey stage reserved for the transaction confirmation / payment selection page'
claims.evidence: ContainerAnalyticsEventState.CHECKOUT_PAGE exists as a real enum value in constants.ts alongside HOMEPAGE, BOOKING_COMPLETION, CUSTOM; source has no further prose description, but the value name and the response's usage in a checkout-page-load scenario is a reasonable, uncontradicted interpretation.

claims.claim: All ContainerModule methods return a response object with a status_code instead of throwing, and 501 means running outside the Grab SuperApp WebView
claims.evidence: Every method in ContainerModule.ts documents status_code values including 501 'Not Implemented: Requires Grab app environment' (e.g. lines 112-116, 227-230, 335-338).

claims.claim: PlatformModule.back() should be used for native back button behavior instead of browser history
claims.evidence: PlatformModule.ts defines a back() method (line 78) with an example matching this usage pattern; plausible and consistent with source, though not deeply inspected.

claims.claim: For custom, non-page-load interactions use ContainerAnalyticsEventState.CUSTOM with a descriptive name and optional data payload, avoiding PII
claims.evidence: CUSTOM is a real enum value in constants.ts; sendAnalyticsEvent's request type supports an optional 'data' field per ContainerModule.ts lines 806-819. The PII caution is reasonable general guidance not directly sourced but not contradicted.

suggestions.assertion: Uses ContainerModule.sendAnalyticsEvent (or equivalent) to fire an analytics event
suggestions.reason: The response hardcodes the string literal 'DEFAULT' instead of importing and referencing the ContainerAnalyticsEventName.DEFAULT constant (it does import ContainerAnalyticsEventState but conspicuously omits ContainerAnalyticsEventName). The assertion as written doesn't catch this minor inconsistency since the string value is correct either way — a stricter assertion could require use of both exported constants for full type-safety, matching the module's own example in ContainerModule.ts.

eval_feedback.overall: All three assertions pass with genuine, verifiable evidence — the response's method names, signatures, and constant values match the ContainerModule and constants.ts source exactly. The task itself (hide back/refresh buttons, set title/background color, fire a checkout-load analytics event) is narrow enough that a correct response almost necessarily satisfies all three assertions together, so the assertions have limited power to distinguish partial success from full success; consider an assertion that also checks the response correctly imports/uses the typed constants (ContainerAnalyticsEventState AND ContainerAnalyticsEventName) rather than accepting raw string literals.
